sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of five articulated middle-caudal dorsal vertebrae collected from the Xinlong Formation in Guangxi Province.
The largest vertebra in this collection, the fifth dorsal, measures 710 mm in total height.
Researchers estimated the full size of Liubangosaurus to be 26 meters long, 5.4 meters tall at the shoulder, and weighing 26 tons.
Sauropod remains were first discovered at the Liubang Quarry in 2001 near Nanning in southern China.
Liubangosaurus was formally described and named in 2010 by Mo Jinyou, Xu Xing, and Eric Buffetaut.
While originally classified only as an eusauropod, later analysis placed Liubangosaurus within the advanced group Somphospondyli.
Liubangosaurus lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
It inhabited a wetland environment during the Early Cretaceous.
Researchers suggested Liubangosaurus may be closely related to the Late Jurassic genus Haplocanthosaurus, but noted this assignment is tentative due to the fragmentary fossil evidence.
The fragmentary nature of Liubangosaurus fossils has complicated scientific determinations of its phylogenetic relationships.
